title: A JMAP VTC capability on the agent, so a client can hold a keyed call
description:
Route (b) of decision mimid-1wgh.114. The half the keying is for.

WHAT IT IS: a capability on the agent's own loopback JMAP endpoint that
lets a client start a call in a chat, learn there is one, and fetch the
call room's media secret for the epoch it is in. The client runs the
media layer's key schedule over that secret, per
draft-atwood-mimi-calls §4.3, and does the media itself. mimid ships no
media stack and no UI (decision mimid-1wgh.38).

WHAT IT SITS ON, all built (bead mimid-1wgh.108): Store::start_call,
Store::media_secret, Room::parent, and the hub's room-policy-04 §5
enforcement.

THE BOUNDARY: the agent's loopback HTTP endpoint with a bearer credential
(docs/design/frontend-auth.md §3), the same one that already carries
plaintext. The secret itself is a MediaSecret: redacted Debug, zeroized
on drop, never written to the database (crates/mimid-agent-core/src/media.rs).
What has NO answer yet is what the JSON looks like, how often a client
may ask, and what it may ask for: one epoch's secret for one room it is
in, and nothing else, is the obvious shape but is not decided.

NEEDS MARK, two things, before the method names exist:
- whether this extends draft-atwood-jmap-vtc or is written fresh. That
  draft already treats a call's chatId as OPTIONAL, which decision
  mimid-1wgh.113 leaned on, so it is the natural home.
- whether the capability is on by default. Every other agent front end
  defaults to loopback, and the JMAP one is on by default; a capability
  that hands out key material may want to be opt-in.

AND REMEMBER: no JMAP goes to the MIMI working group (memory
no-jmap-to-the-mimi-wg). draft-atwood-mimi-calls says where the secret
comes from; it does not and must not mention this surface.
notes:
THE DOCUMENT IS DECIDED: mimid-1wgh.118, extend draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00.md. It is 2394 lines and already complete as an object model; it leaves the E2EE mechanism to the media layer by design, and jmap-vtc-e2ee-guide.md §3 already names MLS as the group key-management answer. What must be added is only the bridge: how a VTCCall relates to a MIMI call room, and how a client gets media_secret. Every write to ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec needs Mark's own OK, one per write. Still open: whether the capability is on by default.
THE DEFAULT IS DECIDED: mimid-1wgh.119, opt-in. Off unless configured, and not advertised in the Session object when off. Revisit once a client implements the extension. Both questions this bead reserved for Mark are now answered (mimid-1wgh.118, mimid-1wgh.119), so what remains is the JSON itself: the method shapes, how often a client may ask, and that it may ask only for one epoch's secret for one room it is in.
THE SPEC HALF IS WRITTEN, 2026-11-23: jmap-chat-spec commit fb05ead, not
yet pushed. Three additions to draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00, 85 lines, and
nothing removed or changed:

- ACCOUNT CAPABILITY supportsMimiKeyedCalls (Boolean, optional), default
  false, which is decision mimid-1wgh.119's opt-in. A server advertising
  false, or omitting it, offers neither of the other two. It is absent or
  false when the MIMI capability is not on the account, since there is
  then no room to key from.
- VTCCall.mimiRoomId (String|null, immutable, server-set), among the
  Optional Binding Fields beside chatId. It names the CALL'S OWN room,
  and the text says plainly that this is not the room of the Chat named
  by chatId: that one is the call room's parent.
- VTCCall/exportMediaSecret, which the text calls out as NOT a standard
  JMAP method, because it returns key material rather than a record and
  its result must not be cached or logged with ordinary responses.
  Arguments accountId, callId, and an optional epoch the client believes
  the group is in, answered with stateMismatch when the group has moved
  on, so a client cannot use a secret for an epoch that ended without
  noticing. Returns epoch and base64 mediaSecret. Carries the draft's
  own MUSTs: input keying material only, never a media key directly;
  derive afresh each epoch; never over an unauthenticated connection,
  never in a push payload or WebSocket event, never retained after
  answering, never sent to another party.
- A §MIMI-Keyed Calls subsection under End-to-End Encrypted Calls,
  stating what the arrangement buys (nothing is sent to key the call;
  membership changes rekey it), why the call needs a room of its own
  (the exported secret belongs to a whole group, so a call keyed from the
  Chat's room is readable by every member of the Chat, undetectably),
  and the cascade window of decision mimid-1wgh.111 with a MUST NOT
  present leaving the Chat as leaving the call.

e2eeEnabled IS UNTOUCHED, as decision mimid-1wgh.118 required.

TWO HOUSE-STYLE FIXES I made to my own text after rendering it: the VTC
draft never says "reject the call" for a method failure, because "call"
means a voice call in that document -- it says "The server MUST return
`forbidden` when ...". My first draft had imported the MIMI binding's
phrasing twice. And RFC4648 and RFC9420 had to be added to the reference
blocks (normative and informative), which xml2rfc caught as unresolved
IDREFs rather than rendering them wrong.

BUILDS CLEAN: kramdown-rfc exit 0, xml2rfc 0 errors.

STILL TO DO HERE: the implementation. Nothing in mimid serves
supportsMimiKeyedCalls, mimiRoomId or VTCCall/exportMediaSecret, and the
agent's JMAP front end has no VTC capability at all. The store half it
sits on is built (Store::start_call, Store::media_secret, Room::parent).
PUSHED 2026-11-23 with Mark's OK: jmap-chat-spec fb05ead on main. Both spec writes of the sweep are up (0f187aa the MIMI binding, fb05ead the VTC draft).
